newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND AND NATAL LOOK CLASSY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND AND NATAL LOOK CLASSY.

text.p: New Zealand's Auckland Blues lead South Africa's Natal Sharks by a point at the top of the Super 12 table after both teams scored impressive wins in the sixth round of matches on Saturday.
Natal were 33-15 winners over Waikato in New Zealand, while Auckland put on a pedigree display to thrash fancied visitors Australian Capital Territories (ACT) 41-9.

Auckland were simply unstoppable against an ACT side which had been tipped to produce an upset. It took a three-try spree by the visitors in the last five minutes to restore some respectability to the scoreline. "Can we just talk about the last five minutes?" asked rueful coach Rod McQueen.
Auckland, who have a game in hand on their nearest rivals, lead the table with 25 points, ahead of Natal (24) and ACT (22).
Natal were also very impressive in dispatching Waikato, proving that some South African sides can travel away from their home shores successfully.
It was a different story for Free State who went down 36-11 to New South Wales in Sydney and failed to score in the second half. But the game will be remembered for a glaring refereeing error.

Free State full-back Jorrie Kruger scored a try in the corner but the referee allowed himself to be overruled by the touch judge who said Kruger had hit the corner flag before grounding the ball. Television replays showed the try was good.

Elsewhere, Queensland's season of woe continued as the Wallaby-packed side went down 47-29 against Wellington. The Hurricanes scored six tries to two to confirm that they are one of the form teams, moving up to fifth place in the process.

Northern Transvaal overcame the odds to snatch a 16-16 draw against former Super 12 leaders Gauteng Lions at Ellis Park. It took a last-minute try from Springbok fly-half Hennie le Roux to earn a share of the spoils for the home side, who have the unenviable task of taking on Auckland at Eden Park next week.
Northerns will play Waikato at Loftus Versfeld with a new coach at the helm. Kitch Christie, who coached South Africa to World Cup triumph two years ago, has been fired after four successive defeats.
Christie will be replaced by John Williams who was removed from his coaching role in favour of Christie at the start of the season.
